craft_notes: Sthāyin: mind as tightened knowing. Sanskrit-first: manas (MIND — kept; single-word line IS the verse's first half); manana-saṃkoca (TIGHTENED-INTO-THOUGHT — kept). Rows: 5 (definition tread: word, then sense — the line-break IS the form), 1 (‘thought’ closes). Close: ‘knowing tightened into thought’. Rupture: the line-break itself (word, then sense — form IS rupture). Rejected: joining lines — killed: word-then-sense is the form; ‘intellect’ — killed: mind kept. Read aloud: MIND — … KNOW-ing TIGHT-ened IN-to THOUGHT.
